record.paper_title: Recent Progress and Open Problems in Algorithmic Convex Geometry
record.original_question: Can one learn a polytope in R^n with m facets in time polynomial in m, n, and 1/ε from random examples, either when the samples are drawn uniformly from the polytope or when they are drawn from a Gaussian distribution and labeled by membership in the polytope?

evidence.quote: Thus an interesting open problem is to learn a polytope in R^n with m facets given either uniform random points from it or from a Gaussian. It is conceivable that the complexity is poly(m, n, 1/ε).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ be an unknown convex polytope defined as the intersection of $m$ halfspaces (so $P$ has at most $m$ facets). Consider the following two learning models, each with accuracy parameter $\varepsilon \in (0,1)$:

(a) Uniform model: the learner receives i.i.d. samples drawn from the uniform distribution on $P$.

(b) Gaussian membership model: the learner receives i.i.d. labeled samples $(x, \mathbf{1}[x \in P])$, where $x \sim \mathcal{N}(0, I_n)$ is the standard $n$-dimensional Gaussian.

In each model, the goal is to output a hypothesis polytope (or set) $\widehat{P}$ such that, with high probability over the samples, the symmetric-difference measure between $\widehat{P}$ and $P$ (with respect to the underlying distribution) is at most $\varepsilon$.

Question: Does there exist a learning algorithm that, in either model (a) or model (b), runs in time polynomial in $m$, $n$, and $1/\varepsilon$ and achieves the above accuracy guarantee?
artifact.status_search_result: Efficiently learning polytopes (intersections of halfspaces) from random samples under natural distributions such as Gaussian remains a central open problem in computational learning theory. The best known algorithms for learning intersections of $k$ halfspaces under Gaussian marginals run in time $n^{\mathrm{poly}\log k}$ or handle only $k = 2^{O(\sqrt{\log n})}$ halfspaces in polynomial time (Klivans–O'Donnell–Servedio), while recent SQ lower bounds rule out fully polynomial algorithms in some agnostic settings. No $\mathrm{poly}(m,n,1/\varepsilon)$ algorithm is known in either the uniform-on-polytope or labeled-Gaussian model.

status_evidence.title: How hard is it to learn an intersection of halfspaces? (Clayton Sanford blog on HSSV22)
status_evidence.snippet: Efficiently learning intersections of halfspaces under Gaussian marginals is one of the most well-studied problems... PAC learning intersections of halfspaces remains unresolved despite much effort.
status_evidence.claim: Problem of efficiently PAC-learning intersections of halfspaces (polytopes) under Gaussian marginals remains open.

status_evidence.title: Learning Intersections of Halfspaces with Distribution Shift (arXiv 2404.02364)
status_evidence.snippet: Prior work either fails in the presence of noise or scales superpolynomially with respect to the dimension.
status_evidence.claim: Known algorithms for learning intersections of halfspaces under Gaussians do not achieve poly(m,n,1/ε) time.

status_evidence.title: A Random Sampling Based Algorithm for Learning Intersections of Halfspaces (Klivans–Servedio–Vempala)
status_evidence.snippet: Algorithms with complexity allowing learning an intersection of up to k=2^{O(sqrt log n)} halfspaces in polynomial time under Gaussian.
status_evidence.claim: Polynomial-time results are known only in restricted regimes, not for general m.
